why: The smallest shop that still runs a real business, and the one where the credit book is the whole business: regulars who pay at the end of the month and a stock list that lives in the owner head.
operator: The owner stands behind the counter, knows every customer by name and keeps the credit in a school notebook. Their day is short but the decisions are constant: what to buy from the wholesaler tomorrow, who owes what, and whether the price still covers the cost. They lose time re-counting, they lose money when a customer moves shop, and they have no idea which items actually make money.
entities: Shop (id, name, branchId, address, phone, currency, openingHours, creditPolicyDays)
Product (id, sku, barcode, nameAr, nameEn, categoryId, unit, unitPricePiasters, costPiasters, taxRate, supplierId, stockQuantity, reorderPoint)
Category (id, nameAr, nameEn, parentId, shelfOrder, iconKey)
CreditCustomer (id, name, phone, whatsappOptIn, creditLimitPiasters, balancePiasters, dueDate, lastPaymentAt, statementSentAt)
CreditEntry (id, customerId, saleId, amountPiasters, kind, createdAt, settledAt, note)
Sale (id, branchId, cashierId, lines, payments, totalPiasters, isCredit, customerId, createdAt, idempotencyKey)
SaleLine (id, saleId, productId, quantity, unitPricePiasters, discountPiasters)
Supplier (id, nameAr, phone, paymentTerms, visitDays, lastOrderAt)
PurchaseOrder (id, supplierId, status, lines, expectedAt, totalPiasters)
Shift (id, branchId, openedBy, openedAt, floatPiasters, closedAt, countedPiasters)
StockCount (id, branchId, countedBy, lines, variancePiasters, countedAt)
Owner (id, name, phone, role, branchId, pinHash)
units: piece, pack, box, kilogram, gram, litre, and a small shop price for the loose item and a pack price for the same product
batches: Usually no. A grocery shop buys in small quantities and sells fast. The pack supports an optional batch only for the shop that sells dairy or frozen, and the expiry is then per batch like the supermarket
expiry: Not a driver here. The shop sees the expiry only where it sells chilled or frozen, and the alert is one line on the stock screen, not a radar
special: The structures specific to this sector are the credit book (a per customer ledger with a limit, a due date and a statement), the customer price list (wholesale price for the regular who buys ten bags, shelf price for the walk in), and the daily note of what was bought from the wholesaler
screens: Counter till: the simplest till in the product, fast on a phone, cash and wallet, and a keypad for the quantities the customer asks for
Credit sale: choose the customer, the screen shows what they still owe and what their limit is, the sale goes on the ledger and the receipt prints with the new balance
Credit book: every customer with the balance, the limit, the oldest unpaid entry and the due date, sorted by how late it is
Statement: the month statement for one customer, printable and sendable on WhatsApp, with the items, the amounts and the payments received
Stock list: what is left, what it cost, what it sells for, and the margin for each item
Buy from the wholesaler: the list of what ran low with the last price, send it to the supplier on WhatsApp or print it
End of day: the money counted against the sales, the credit given today listed, and the profit that is real after the cost of the goods
Regular customer: what this customer buys, how often, what they owe and one tap to message them
roles: Owner: everything, including the credit book, the pricing and the staff
Cashier: sells, takes payment, records a credit sale, cannot raise the credit limit
Assistant: sells and counts, no access to the credit book and no price changes
reports: Money in the drawer today against the sales of today
The credit book: total owed, the top ten debtors, the oldest unpaid entry
What makes money: margin per item, so the owner stops selling the items that lose
What ran low this week: the buy list for the wholesaler
Who comes back: the customers with a purchase every week and what they buy
Waste and shrink: the counted difference per item
integrations: Thermal printer through ESC/POS, optional because many shops print on the phone
Barcode scanner in keyboard mode, optional because the owner types the code
WhatsApp for the statement to the customer and the buy list to the wholesaler, through the shop own account
Daily backup of the sales and the credit book to the cloud with the offline queue
onboarding: Business basics: name, address, phone, currency and the opening hours
Shelves: pick the categories the shop has and set the order
Credit policy: the number of days a regular may pay later, and whether the shop wants a limit per customer
Regulars: add the first credit customers with a phone number and a limit
Stock: add the items the shop sells most, with the cost and the price
First week plan: print one receipt, open the credit book, count the drawer at close, add the wholesaler
seed: Category list in Arabic for a neighbourhood grocery: vegetables, fruit, bread, dairy, eggs, rice and pasta, oils, sugar, tea and coffee, water, snacks, household, cleaning
A unit list with the loose and the pack price on the same item
An empty credit customer list, never seeded with fake names
A receipt layout with the shop header and the credit line that shows the new balance
A short buying list template the owner can print and take to the wholesaler

landing_ar.headline: بقالة بتفوق على ذاكرتها: دفتر العملاء، والشراء من الجملة، وختام اليوم
landing_ar.sub: كاشير سريع على الموبايل، دفتر آجل للزبون الثابت، وقائمة الشراء جاهزة للجملة كل يوم

landing_en.headline: A grocery shop that runs on more than memory: the credit book, the wholesaler list and the end of the day
landing_en.sub: A fast till on the phone, a credit book for the regulars, and a buying list that writes itself when stock runs low
benefits: The notebook becomes a screen: every credit customer with the balance and the due date in one place
The buying list for the wholesaler writes itself from what ran low
You see which items make money and which ones you are giving away
faq: Can it work with no connection? Yes: selling continues, debts are recorded, and everything syncs when the connection is back
Does the credit book charge interest? No: it is a shop ledger, with no interest, no collections and no loans

pricing: The free tier is enough for one person behind the counter: one business, one branch, two seats, the till and the credit book
Starter adds a year of history and five seats for the shop with a helper
The Business tier adds the buying list from the velocity, the stock count by phone camera and the statements by WhatsApp
The credit book is never behind the highest tier: a grocery shop that cannot see its own debts is a grocery shop in trouble

tasks.title: Register the grocery shop pack in the sector registry
tasks.brief: Add the manifest for grocery-shop in packages/core/src/sectors/registry.ts with the id, the Arabic and English names, the base template market, the modules it turns on (pos, inventory, credits, customers, shifts), the feature flags, the role templates and the terminology map.
tasks.done: getSector('grocery-shop') returns the manifest and the registry test asserts the modules and the roles.

tasks.title: Write the credit book data model
tasks.brief: Type the credit entities in packages/core/src/sectors/grocery-shop/schema.ts: credit customer with limit and due date, credit entry with kind, settlement and note, and the sale flag that points a sale at a customer. Validate that a sale cannot exceed the limit without an explicit override that is audited.
tasks.done: The schema compiles, the validation rejects a sale over the limit, and the tests for the limit, the settlement and the statement balance pass.

tasks.title: Build the grocery seed with the Arabic category list
tasks.brief: Write packages/core/src/sectors/grocery-shop/seed.ts with the neighbourhood grocery categories in Arabic, the unit list with loose and pack prices, the receipt layout with the credit balance line, and the buying list template. No customer is ever seeded.
tasks.done: The seed loads, the test asserts the category list and that the credit customer list is empty.

tasks.title: Write the grocery terminology map in Arabic and English
tasks.brief: Create packages/ui/src/sector/grocery-shop/glossary.ts with the words a neighbourhood shop uses: الآجل, الدفتر, الكاشير, الجملة, التالف, the till words and the receipt words, in Arabic and English.
tasks.done: The glossary covers every screen of the sector with no generic retail wording and the label test passes on the rendered till.

tasks.title: Build the credit sale flow on the counter till
tasks.brief: Add the credit path to the till: pick the customer, see the balance and the limit before the sale is confirmed, block or escalate over the limit, and print the receipt with the new balance and the due date.
tasks.done: A credit sale records the entry, updates the balance, refuses over the limit without the manager override, and the printed receipt shows the new balance.

tasks.title: Build the credit book screen and the statement
tasks.brief: Build the credit book: customers sorted by how late the oldest unpaid entry is, with the balance, the limit and the due date, plus a monthly statement view for one customer that prints and sends on WhatsApp.
tasks.done: The book lists every customer with a balance, the statement totals match the entries, and the send action produces a shareable message.

tasks.title: Build the buying list from the low stock screen
tasks.brief: Build the screen that lists what ran low with the last purchase price and the quantity to order, and prints the list for the wholesaler or sends it on WhatsApp. The suggestion uses the real sales velocity and never orders on its own.
tasks.done: The list names the items that ran low with a price from the last purchase order, and the quantity comes from the last thirty days of sales.

tasks.title: Build the end of day screen for this sector
tasks.brief: Build the close of day: money counted against money expected, the credit given today listed with the customers, the cost of the goods sold and the real margin, so the owner sees the truth after the shutters come down.
tasks.done: The screen shows cash against sales, the credit list of today and the margin, and the numbers match a manual calculation in the test.

tasks.title: Write the margin and shrink report pack
tasks.brief: Add the reports of this sector: margin per item, the total of the credit book, the top debtors, the money in the drawer against the sales, the waste and shrink from the stock count, each with the CSV export.
tasks.done: Every report returns its own numbers from the business documents, the test matches a manual calculation and the export opens in a spreadsheet.

tasks.title: Publish the grocery shop landing page in Arabic and English
tasks.brief: Build the sector page from the outline: the Arabic headline first, the credit book and the buying list as the two proof blocks with real screenshots, the two questions answered, and the English mirror.
tasks.done: The page passes the layout rules at 320 to 1920 px in both languages and both themes, and no promise appears that the pack does not deliver.

risks: The credit book is a shop ledger, so no interest, no instalments, no collection agency and no legal claim is built into it
Customer names are personal data of the shop, so they never enter our analytics and can be exported or deleted from the settings
The margin report depends on real purchase costs, so an item without a cost is shown as missing a cost instead of being counted as zero
No wholesaler name or price is published in our copy: the supplier data belongs to the shop
